task: This is more of a job for an engineer than a ranger. We need to install an Edelweiss radio device on the uninhabited planet of <ToPlanet>. We have no permanent communication with our new research base due to the sandstorms caused by the star <ToStar>'s hyperactivity. This powerful apparatus will fix our radio communications with the orbital hyper-transmitter. Of course, you won't be alone at the base. Our geologist will be with you. We trust that <Money> cr. is a sufficient fee, despite your predecessor’s recent death under unclear circumstances. Will you handle this mission in the next <Day> days?
success:
Welcome back, <Ranger>!
It's not all that simple with this geological station, you know! Two corpses, which had been discovered, baffled the newly arrived personnel. However we both know that this is just a horrible result of safety rules violation! While the discovery of gold nuggets in the stomachs of annelus creepers literally turned the station into our most profitable geological research enterprise.
You've acted swiftly - and we appreciate that. Thanks to the permanent communication with the station, we work much more effectively with our personnel, despite the raging storms. And according to the contract, you receive <Money> cr. Good luck, ranger!
loc.2.0: The bunkroom is quite cozy, with every kind of convenience and a medical device on the wall. It also has a modern radio station. There is a computer on the table, it stores all the equipment schemes, various kinds of instructions, and some password-protected video file.
loc.2.1: The computer, as usual, is on the table. The medical device on the wall heartily welcomes you with the green light of its stand-by mode.
loc.2.3: Someone ransacked the bunkroom and <clr> broke the medical device<clrEnd>.
loc.2.4: This multi-tool can do more than just drive in screws, breaking locks with it isn't a big problem.
loc.2.5:
You enter the gaalian ranger's badge number, and the file opens.
The video showed a bunkroom, nearly the same as yours, except for a large, concave table with a drain. The dissected body of a huge worm is lying on the table. Thick liquid flows from its wounds into the drain. The frightened face of a Gaal squeezes into the frame: 
"Guyolak isn't a xeno-zoologist, he keeps bringing new and different creepers," the Gaal whispers. "I suspected something was wrong right from the start. I'll send this file with the next supply ship. Oh, yes. And here's another surprise." The engineer directed the camera at a metal case and then <clr>opened the door marked with 2, then the third one, then the first, and the second again<clrEnd>. Something clicked and the Gaal was about to show what was inside, but the sound of steps in the corridor interrupted him. - Ah, looks like Guyolak is coming...
"End of file. To watch the file again, please re-enter the password," you were prompted by the computer.
loc.2.6:
1. The installation site must meet a number of requirements (a long list of requirements follows)
...
Use of a standard geological multipurpose analyzer is recommended.
2. Set the Edelweiss unit in its place (see item 1) without removing the factory packaging.
3. Make sure that items 1 and 2 of this manual have been fulfilled and press the 'Install' button located in the opening on the front panel of the Edelweiss unit's factory packaging.
4. Perform a test connection with a remote user through any nearby radio center.
loc.2.7: A couple of manipulators slid quickly along your body, making staccato injections in specific locations. The effect is immediate - your health is completely restored.
loc.3.0: The well-lit corridor is empty. Only the shallow drumming of rubble and the hissing of sand on the station cover break the silence. The storm is still raging outside.
loc.3.1:
You enter the corridor. Suddenly the lock chamber doors swish open and something huge tumbles inside. It's a hydraulic spacesuit for walking on the surface of planets with severe environmental conditions. Its owner, a Fae who is quite strong for his race, drags a disgusting one-and-a-half-meter worm. A sticky trail of blood is flowing out of a <clr>wound on the side of the worm<clrEnd>. Not noticing you, the Fae quickly connects the spacesuit to a special charging device on the wall with some equipment and goes outside. At first, he was startled by your greeting, but then he smiled wryly and introduced himself, 
"Guyolak, geologist."
"<Ranger>, ranger and temporarily engineer at this station."
"Okay, then. You do your thing, and I'll do mine." The Fae picks the worm up by its tail, drags it to his laboratory, and slams the door.
loc.3.2: As usual, the corridor is empty. Your footsteps echo loudly in the silence.
loc.3.3: There's nobody in the corridor. The noise of the storm outside interrupts the silence.
loc.3.4: The light of a lamp streams down the empty corridor, not foreshadowing anything fearful.
loc.4.0: You grope along a wasteland flooded with the red light. The pungent smell of ammonia makes you sick, and the wind throws sand into your face. It's difficult to find your way without a radar.
loc.4.1: You grope along a wasteland flooded with red light. The pungent smell of ammonia makes you ill, and the wind beats sand into your face. It's difficult to find your way without radar.
loc.4.2: You grope along a wasteland flooded with red light. The pungent smell of ammonia makes you ill, and the wind beats sand into your face. It's difficult to find your way without radar.
loc.4.3: You grope through the storm, choking on the ammonia-saturated air. You have to rely on your memory, because the spacesuit doesn't have radar.

loc.4.6: You can't figure out which way to go because of the poor visibility caused by the sand and dust blowing all around. The spacesuit's oxygen supply is limited, so wandering around is dangerous.

loc.5.0: You ascend the ladder, put your hand to the scanner, and open the door. All systems are functioning. You're ready for takeoff right away.
loc.5.1: You land the ship in the station hangar. The doors above the ship close, and the dust and harmful impurities are pumped out of the air.
loc.5.2: You ascend the ladder and are about to put your hand to the scanner when you suddenly notice that the <clr>door is already opened<clrEnd>. But you don't see anything suspicious inside. All systems are operational. You're ready for a takeoff right away.
loc.5.3: You land the ship in the station hangar.
loc.26.0: The doors close, and the lock chamber falls silent.
loc.26.1: As soon as the external gate closes, the pumps start up. The air is cleared of impurities and dust, and you can inhale the pure air freely.
loc.26.2: You connect the charging device to a special jack on the spacesuit's chest panel. The hoses strain from the pressure, but soon the charging system shuts down with a sharp click. The indicator lights signal that all is in order.
loc.27.0: Heat from your ship's engines is spreading throughout the small hangar. The door from here leads into a corridor that connects all the rooms of the station.
loc.27.1: Your ship is in the small hanger, ready for a takeoff.
loc.28.0: You are at a stand with various geological equipment.
loc.28.1: After checking that its reserves are okay, you squash into a heavy spacesuit and turn it on.
loc.28.2: You deftly get out of the spacesuit and plug it into the charging device. It starts whistling, replenishes the spacesuit's reserves, and then switches off.
loc.28.3: You pick up the analyzer. This rather heavy device can show where the Edelweiss unit can be installed in order to provide permanent communication, the soil should be firm, thus preventing the device from sinking down in the soil.
loc.28.4:
You put down the Edelweiss and pick up the analyzer.
The device consists of a heavy case equipped with the Violet Fang system, which transmits the data directly to a portable radar. However, its main function is to indicate a place with sufficiently firm soil where the Edelweiss can be installed in order to provide a stable connection.
loc.28.5: You pick up the box with the Edelweiss unit.
loc.28.6: They are too heavy to carry at the same time. You put down the analyzer case, and pick up the box with the Edelweiss unit.
loc.28.7: The <clr>Edelweiss unit is missing<clrEnd> from the equipment rack!
loc.28.8: All the equipment is there <clr>but the spacesuit!<clrEnd>
loc.28.9: You connect the charging device to a special jack on the spacesuit's chest panel. The hoses strain from the pressure, but soon the charging system shut down with a sharp click. The indicator lights signaled that all was in order.
loc.29.0: The door to the geologist's bunkroom is locked, and nobody answers.
loc.29.1:
The screwdriver rustling in the lock made the geologist open the door and nearly choke at your boldness: 
"What the ...! What do you think you are doing?!" He quickly returns with a portable circular saw. If I ever see you messing with my lock again, I'll slice you to pieces!
"Hey... Pardon me, I just thought I saw cockroach slipping into the keyhole. So I wanted to..." You draw a horizontal line across your neck with the screwdriver.
"Uh-huh. You're a terrible liar. But I'm not joking. Make sure I don't meet you at my door again," said Guyolak, threatening you with the circular saw.
loc.29.2: You hear a circular saw can heard from time to time behind the door. But the geologist obviously isn't going to open the door.
loc.29.3: The door with number {[p28]} opens, but you find nothing useful in this compartment.
loc.29.4: You are in the middle of the geologist's bunkroom. The nauseating sight of the remains of a worm on a dissection table suppresses any desire to stay here.
loc.29.5: The box with the Edelweiss unit is covered with a cloth on the bottom shelf of the rack.
loc.29.6: Based on the information on the panel, you realize that most of the samples taken from the annulus creeper's stomach are gold nuggets! But you don’t find the precious metal itself anywhere nearby.
loc.29.7: A secret compartment in the cabinet opens. It is holding a circular saw inside, which soon made its way into your hands.
loc.29.8: You find only slime and fine slices of the worm under the table.
loc.29.9: With the kind of screwdriver you have, this wasn't difficult. The door swings open and you are greeted with a disgusting sight: the worm's remains are lying on the table. The Fae has literally turned this formerly-dangerous predator inside out. Puddles of slime shine on the floor, and there are slippery stains on the walls.
loc.40.0:
The force of sand and dust hisses against the roof of the ship, but you soon leave the storm area and land and a quiet region of planet <ToPlanet>.
You're safe, but you <clr>failed your mission<clrEnd>.
loc.41.0:
After leaving the dense clouds of sand and dust below, you are able to contact the head of the research department. He looks at you attentively. 
"Is there something you'd like to ask me or tell me, <Ranger>?
loc.41.1: "You need to install the Edelweiss radio unit so we can communicate with the station despite the furious sandstorms. It's vital that you wear the spacesuit to avoid being poisoned in <ToPlanet>'s atmosphere. And you need to have a radar device with you, otherwise it's easy to get lost. There should be detailed instructions in your bunkroom on how to install the radio unit."
loc.41.2:
"Hmmm. It's very strange, but Guyolak insists that he won't come out until <ToStar>'s hyperactivity ends. And these storms seem to be related to it. Maybe he's trying to find our gaalian engineer? But that's entirely pointless, because no humanoid could stay on the planet's surface that long without a supply of pure air."
"For some reason, Guyolak dragged in another huge worm! Why do you think he's doing this?"
"Perhaps he's just hunting? You got to do something with yourself if you can't work on research full-time. Better ask him yourself."
loc.41.3:
"So it seems this engineer left the station without radar?" asks the chief in amazement.
"Yes. That's what Guyolak told me. What's more, he had his device!" you said, holding up your radar wrist unit. One can only guess how he got it and why the Gaal forgot about the safety measures.
"Don't worry, <Ranger>. There are probably simple and clear explanations for this. The important thing is that you install the communication link and investigate the circumstances of your predecessor’s death."
loc.41.4:
"I huge worm attacked me! You didn't warn me that this mission would be dangerous! How are you going to cover these risks?" 
"Just a minute..." the chief said and bent over the monitor on his table, running his eyes over some files. "You have the right to terminate the contract, but you won't receive any compensation for your injuries or the time you've spent here. To receive the agreed amount, you have to install the radio unit." With that, the chief throws up his hands as if he's helpless to change the situation.
loc.41.5:
You describe your careful discovery. The chief looks at you sympathetically. 
"I'm very sorry you had to go through that. Nevertheless, you must fulfill your contractual obligations before you leave the station.
"The Gaals' air supply has been cut off. I think we're dealing with a murder, here."
"Give it up! You're not a criminal forensics expert, <Ranger>. Don't make such serious accusations. Leave this to the professionals... Of course, our government can't send a special expedition right now. Let's just hope for the best going forward."
loc.41.6: "Perfect. Just a mere formality remains. I need you to connect with me from your bunkroom, <Ranger>. Then we can consider this job done!"
loc.41.7:
"That won't do. How did you lose your spacesuit?" asks the chief reproachfully.
"Guyolak took it. So how am I to install the Edelweiss unit now?"
"Hmmm... You look like a strong enough young man, <Ranger>. You're probably healthy enough to drag the radio unit even without a spacesuit."
"Are you joking?!"
"Not at all. The members of the first expedition did that many times."
"And how many of them survived?"
Back at the station, the official flips through some data sheets. "60%. I think that's a pretty good percentage."
loc.41.8: "Of course, to go under the surface of a severe planet like <ToPlanet> you should have a spacesuit, but it is possible without one. The important thing is to only have brief exposure to the poisonous atmosphere and to have timely medical attention."
loc.42.0:
The chief geological researcher from planet <FromPlanet> came on the line, gave you the coordinates of the station, and began to bring you up to speed on the situation. 
"They probably warned you, <Ranger>, that conditions on this planet are extremely severe. The sandstorms are so strong you can't even have a radio conversation with station personnel. Lately, all communication has been made exclusively through supply ships. Your mission is to install the Edelweiss radio unit to establish stable communications. Your predecessor's attempt to do this ended dramatically: He died mysteriously while outside the station," said the chief, pondering something for a moment.
A blood-red glow was all that could be seen through the viewports. The crimson sand and dust that was raging through the air prevented the <ToStar>'s rays from penetrating. Flying was only possible using instruments. At last, the outline of the base appeared on the radar. The chief continued,
"The geologist Guyolak should be at the station right now. He flat-out refuses to come up to the surface when it's stormy like this. He'll bring you up to speed on everything. And if you need to know anything else, I'm at your service. Good luck! Over and out."
You lose altitude quickly and land in the small geological station's covered hangar. The doors above the ship close. Then the dust and harmful impurities are pumped out of the air.

loc.67.0: The blow is powerful and exact. The worm arches, begins trembles, and then becomes still. You cautiously get out of the quicksand and cast an apprehensive glance at the predator's corpse.
loc.67.1: You nearly trip over something. It's the body of a Gaal in a spacesuit. He's frozen as if attempting to shout, clutching his throat with his hands. You examine the corpse as carefully as the dim light of <ToStar> allows. The hose supplying oxygen to the his spacesuit has been severed.  He suffocated to death. After opening the spacesuit, you find a ranger badge and serial number on the wearer's jacket. <clr>You record the number,<clrEnd> just in case.
loc.67.2: The analyzer emits a pleasant sound, indicating that your current location satisfies the installation requirements for the radio unit.
loc.67.3: Relieved, you put down the box and press the "Install" button. The panels on the packaging open and the mechanism releases several supports, which immediately go deep into the soil. The swollen bud of folded antennas extends its petals to form a sort of flower. The flower's head performs some scanning motions and then stands still, apparently having discovered the best position for reception.
loc.67.4: You evade the geologist's blows and kick at him powerfully in return. The Fae takes a blow in the stomach and falls, dripping froth from his mouth onto the sand.
loc.67.5: Guyolak tries to grab your throat, but you thrust the saw forward and turn it on... The offensive sound of the bones being cut asunder muffles the howls of the storm. Guyolak goes limp and falls onto the red sand.
loc.68.0: Suddenly, your legs disappear into the sand. You struggle with all your might, but you are helplessly stuck. A huge worm emerges from the soil. You can't escape, but you've got to do something!
loc.68.1: Waiting for the right moment, you strike the worm on its head. It's as hard as concrete. In response, the creeper gives you a strong bite.
loc.68.2: The creeper manages to open its jaws and bite your arm, causing you great pain.
loc.68.3: The worm's back is unprotected. You strike, leaving it with just {[p28]*30}% of its health.
loc.68.4: The screwdriver cuts badly into the worm's neck, leaving it with {[p28]*30}% of its health.
loc.68.5: In your struggle to escape, you find yourself sinking deeper into the sand. The worm manages to creep around behind you. It bites you severely in the back.
loc.72.0: The door opening is too small for your spacesuit to pass through!
loc.72.1: The spacesuit is too big - it's preventing you from going through the door.
loc.72.2: You must remove the spacesuit to pass through the door.
loc.72.3: You must remove the spacesuit to pass through the door. You can do that at the equipment rack.
loc.74.0:
Something hits you in the back! Turning around, you see Guyolak wearing a spacesuit. He's brandishing a stick at you. 
"Heh, heh. You weren't expecting that were you, <Ranger>? Neither did your predecessor. He kept trying to set up the communication link and nose into what I was doing, so he could snitch on me... " said the geologist, pointing somewhere upward with his stick. The wind muffled the geologist's spiteful panting, but he went on: "You're already a dead man, and you'll take my little secret with you. The creepers are natural gold-miners - they find nuggets and devour them like sharks. I don't know if they need it for digestion or what, but you can always find gold in their stomachs!"
loc.74.1:
In response to your peaceful gesture, the geologist laughed haughtily and walloped you with the stick. 
"Are all rangers so stupid that they can't understand it takes some serious motivation to go out into weather like this? Personally, gold is worth the risk - and not just to my own life!" The scowl on his face told you he was prepared to kill anyone for the contemptible metal.
loc.74.2: You deliver a series of blows, but most of them hit the hard parts of his spacesuit. Guyolak bursts out laughing and again brings the stick down on your head.
loc.74.4: You manage to kick Guyolak in the unprotected area of the stomach. It hurt the Fae - a lot.
loc.76.0: The speakers emit only an annoying "Psh-psh-psh-psh" sound. You can't make out anything because of all the interference.
loc.77.0:
It isn't the most crisp picture, but the signal is stable enough to communicate with planet <FromPlanet>. "Oh, I see you've connected from your bunkroom!" said the chief researcher, beaming with satisfaction. Then he became somewhat deflated. "I've been trying to contact the geologist, but Guyolak isn't responding. Do you know why?"
He went out onto the surface and… didn't say anything about returning," you said without going into all the details of your last encounter with the geologist.
"Hmmm... That is really strange. Well, we've found a permanent replacement for you. He should be at the station tomorrow morning and he'll be able to figure everything out., Well, you've established the connection, so you can come for your reward. We'll be waiting for you, <Ranger>!
"Okay. Until then."
After turning off the transmitter, your head toward the hangar. You find a box of <clr>gold nuggets<clrEnd> on the ramp – the geologist was clearly preparing to fly away on your ship.
loc.82.0: After hearing your knock, the geologist opens the door slightly and looks at you questioningly.
loc.82.1:
Guyolak only scowls. 
"Blah, blah, blah-blity, blah...get to the point, <clr>Little<clrEnd> <Ranger>!
"<Ranger>," you correct him.
"It doesn't matter. Say what you need or get out of here."
loc.82.2:
Guyolak's eyes narrow, then he suddenly puts on an affected grin. 
"Heh, heh. It's quite simple. The blockhead went out <clr>onto the surface with no radar and got lost<clrEnd>. And sandstorms aren't very forgiving of blunders." The geologist carelessly brushes away a slimy slice of a worm and stares at you.
loc.82.3: "The annulus creeper is a local predator. The creepers cover large distances underground. For me, they're like a natural probe that extends the area of my research. Their hairs pick up grit at all sorts of depths, and their stomachs have..." Just then the geologist hesitated and changed the subject. If you’re talking about the one you saw in my bunkroom, it's as harmless as a snowman in the spring. Believe me."
loc.82.4: "That doesn't concern me. You're an engineer; <clr>you've got equipment, a computer<clrEnd> - so, go right ahead! You're not expecting me to do your job, are you? I've got enough trouble without any permanent radio communication with <FromPlanet>..." said Guyolak, nervously drumming his fingers on the door frame.
loc.82.5: "Man, you are really obnoxious. Do your job, and I'll do mine. And you don't need to go breaking into my bunkroom: after all, I've got a right to privacy, too.  Guyolak folds his arms across his chest and frowns.
loc.82.6: "Uh," said the fae, faltering for a moment. That creeper wouldn't let me sleep with its constant scratching at the bottom of my bunkroom, so I neutralized it.
loc.82.7:
"Ah. So that's what you're after. Just a second..." The geologist retreats deep into the bunkroom, and through the open door you can see slime stains on the floor as well as a worm tail drooping from the table. "Here you go!" said Guyolak, offering you a flat device with fasteners. But then he intentionally dropped it to your feet. "Oops," said the malicious Fae, apparently deriving satisfaction from this. "Don't you worry. It's shockproof... Probably." The geologist bursts into disgusting laughter. 
<clr>You pick up the radar unit<clrEnd>, which turns to out to be okay. You attach it to your arm.
loc.88.0: "Hold on, <Ranger>! You encounter more difficult tasks in your everyday service. Please help us install the radio unit," begs the official.
